validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: confirmed independently by 3 distinct-origin sources. (1) Intergas Central Asia's own official capacity register 'Информация о наличии существующей мощности Магистральных Газопроводов АО Интергаз Центральная Азия (по состоянию 01.01.2025г)' lists 'Окарем-Бейнеу' as an operating trunk ('магистральный') gas pipeline, 1200mm nominal dia, commissioned 1972-1974, with a nonzero 2024 utilized throughput (3,100 mln m3/y, 88% listed utilization) — i.e. it is definitely real and definitely operating, straight from the operator. (2) dknews.kz (26 Jun 2023, independent news outlet) explicitly names 'магистральный газопровод «Окарем – Бейнеу»' as the pipeline the 40-year-old 'Zhanaozen-Zhetybai-Aktau' system is a continuation of, supplying Mangystau oblast/Aktau/industry. (3) primeminister.kz (23 Oct 2023, KZ government press office) independently references 'газопровод «Окарем-Бейнеу»' and its historical throughput. Classification as transmission ('магистральный' = trunk) is explicit in source (1) and (2), not inferred. START YEAR 1974 matches source (1)'s stated commissioning window '1972-1974' exactly (upper bound) and is consistent with dknews' 'эксплуатируется уже более 40 лет' as of 2023 (2023-1974=49 yrs, fits). DIAMETER 1020/1220mm (GEM, actual OD in mm) reconciles exactly with source (1)'s '1200'/'1000' nominal-diameter (Ду) listing for the mainline vs its parallel loop — DN1200 pipe has 1220mm OD and DN1000 pipe has 1020mm OD, standard Russian/Soviet GOST pipe-size convention (nominal vs actual bore), so this is NOT a diameter discrepancy, just two different diameter-naming conventions for the same two pipe classes. CAVEAT: source (1) shows Okarem-Beyneu is actually TWO parallel physical lines commissioned in the same 1972-1974 window — the 1200mm/309.8km mainline AND a separate 1000mm/233km 'Лупинг Окарем-Бейнеу' (loop) — which is consistent with GEM's single P2492 row listing both diameters together, but see the Length/Capacity concerns below: GEM's LengthKnown and Capacity do not match either line individually or their sum. OWNER: Owner1=Turkmengaz / Owner2=Samruk-Kazyna SWF JSC is directionally right but imprecisely sourced for this specific segment — kase.kz confirms QazaqGaz (KZTG) is the Samruk-Kazyna-linked national gas company, and intergas.kz 'About the company' confirms Intergas Central Asia (the operator named in source (1)) is a subsidiary running Kazakhstan's main gas pipeline system; Turkmengaz as the Turkmen-side owner is a reasonable but not explicitly-sourced-for-this-pipeline inference (Turkmengaz is Turkmenistan's national gas company and would plausibly own the TM segment). Treat Owner as medium confidence, not high.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC — LENGTH, material disagreement. GEM's current LengthKnown=999.00 km has NO citation attached (MISSING_REF) and does not survive contact with the pipeline operator's own register. Intergas Central Asia's 'Информация о наличии существующей мощности...по состоянию 01.01.2025г' (a Q4-2024 capacity report, i.e. current, primary, and authoritative — this is the entity that physically runs the Kazakh gas trunk network) lists TWO distinct physical lines under this name: 'Окарем-Бейнеу' mainline = 1200mm / 309.8 km / commissioned 1972-1974 / design 8,260 mln m3/y / actual-2024 3,100 mln m3/y; and a parallel 'Лупинг Окарем-Бейнеу' (loop) = 1000mm / 233 km / same 1972-1974 window / design 4,020 mln m3/y / actual-2024 3,290 mln m3/y. Neither figure (309.8, 233) nor their sum (542.8 km) comes anywhere close to 999 km — off by roughly 3.2x on the single line, or 1.8x even combined. This also fits the wider network logic checked against 2 independent secondary sources (en.wikipedia.org CAC infobox + karakalpak-karakalpakstan.blogspot.com, both describing the whole CAC system's 'western branch'/CAC-3 running from Okarem, Turkmenistan north through Beyneu to Alexandrov Gay, Russia, ~2,000 km total): Beyneu is a mid-route junction, not an endpoint of a ~1,000 km stand-alone segment — gas arriving at Beyneu from Turkmenistan splits further, part continuing NORTH toward Russia (the P2291/P2292/P5770/P5771 'Central Asia-Center' family) and part heading SOUTH to Zhanaozen/Aktau for local Mangystau supply (P5772 'Beyneu-Zhanaozen' + the P3948 Zhanaozen-Zhetybai-Aktau family) — consistent with dknews.kz explicitly calling Zhanaozen-Zhetybai-Aktau 'a continuation of' Okarem-Beyneu. A ~310 km Turkmenistan-to-Beyneu run is the coherent, internally-consistent read; 999 km is not. I could not find a second numeric-length source pinpointing exactly 309.8/233 km (verifier's automated content-check fails on this specific PDF for every ASCII token tried — '309,8', '1972-1974', '1972', even 'Интергаз' — despite a clean HTTP 200; this matches the documented url_verifier caveat that a content FAIL on a PDF proves nothing, and I confirmed the text is genuinely present via `pdftotext -layout` locally: the extracted row reads verbatim 'Окарем-Бейнеу 1200 309,8 1972-1974 8 260 3 100 88%'), so I'm treating the length correction as high-confidence on a single strong primary/operator source rather than double-independently-numerically-confirmed. Recommend Update apply the correction and note the untracked loop line to the redundancy-cluster/discovery leg.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC — CAPACITY, material disagreement. Current value 3.78 bcm/y is HAS_REF (primeminister.kz + ppt-online.org), but ppt-online.org already fails the automated value check (doesn't contain '3.78'), and primeminister.kz's actual text does NOT say 3.78 either — it says the pre-existing Okarem-Beyneu route 'обеспечивал прокачку чуть более 3 млрд куб. метров' ('provided throughput of just over 3 billion cubic meters') before the 2023 second-line (P5772) addition. That figure — 'just over 3' — lines up almost exactly with Intergas' own 2024 actual/utilized throughput of 3,100 mln m3/y (3.10 bcm/y) for the Okarem-Beyneu mainline, not 3.78. Intergas' register also gives a DESIGN capacity of 8,260 mln m3/y (8.26 bcm/y) for the same line. So two independent origins (KZ PM's press office and the pipeline operator) agree the throughput commonly discussed for 'Okarem-Beyneu' is ~3.1 bcm/y (actual), while the nameplate/design figure is 8.26 bcm/y — and GEM's 3.78 sits awkwardly between the two, matching neither cleanly (+22% over actual, -54% under design). This batch's own convention (per the orchestrator's KMG-register cross-check on Saryarka) is that GEM's Capacity field tracks design/nameplate capacity, which would argue for 8.26, not 3.78 — but I'm flagging rather than silently overwriting since I can't rule out 3.78 reflecting some other cited scope (e.g. a stage or a unit-conversion slip) that I haven't identified. Do not carry the existing ppt-online.org citation forward uncritically; it's a construction-progress presentation about the SECOND line (per its own title 'Строительство 2-ой ники участка Бейнеу-Жанаозен МГ Окарем-Бейнеу'), i.e. about P5772, not a capacity source for P2492 itself.
